prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A gradiometer system including one or more magnetic sensor(s) is disclosed. The gradiometer includes an actuation module connectable to the magnetic sensor(s) to vary one or more sensing positions at which a magnetic field is sensed thereby. The one or more sensing positions are varied according to a certain displacement function indicating a predetermined displacement between the sensing positions as a function of time. A controller of the gradiometer system is adapted to determine at least one vector component of a gradient of the magnetic field sensed by the sensor(s) by carrying out the following: (i) obtaining readout data from the sensor(s) indicative of the magnetic field sensed at the varied sensing positions during a certain measurement time duration; (ii) processing the readout data to determine a differential magnetic field time profile indicating a difference between the magnetic fields sensed at at least two of the sensing positions during the measurement time duration; and (iii) demodulating the differential magnetic field time profile in accordance with the displacement function to thereby determine a demodulated time profile indicative of the at least one vector component of the gradient of the measured magnetic field.

outputs.L1: A gradiometer system comprising one or more magnetic sensors is disclosed. The gradiometer includes an actuation module connectable to the magnetic sensor(s) and configured to vary one or more sensing positions at which the magnetic field is sensed. The sensing positions are varied according to a displacement function that defines a predetermined displacement between the sensing positions as a function of time. A controller of the gradiometer system is configured to determine at least one vector component of a gradient of the magnetic field sensed by the sensor(s) by: (i) obtaining readout data from the sensor(s) indicative of the magnetic field sensed at the varied sensing positions over a specified measurement duration; (ii) processing the readout data to determine a differential magnetic-field time profile representing a difference between the magnetic fields sensed at at least two of the sensing positions during the measurement duration; and (iii) demodulating the differential magnetic-field time profile in accordance with the displacement function, thereby determining a demodulated time profile indicative of the at least one vector component of the gradient of the measured magnetic field.
outputs.L2:
A gradiometer system is described that uses at least one magnetic sensor. The system includes an actuation module coupled, or capable of being coupled, to the magnetic sensor or sensors. This module changes one or more locations at which the magnetic field is detected. The sensing locations are moved according to a specified displacement function that defines a predetermined separation between the locations over time.

The system further includes a controller configured to calculate at least one vector component of the gradient of the sensed magnetic field. To do so, the controller: (i) receives sensor readout data representing magnetic-field measurements taken at the changing sensing locations during a defined measurement interval; (ii) analyzes the data to generate a differential magnetic-field time profile representing the difference between fields measured at two or more sensing locations during that interval; and (iii) demodulates the differential time profile using the displacement function, producing a demodulated time profile that represents the at least one vector component of the measured magnetic-field gradient.
outputs.L3:
The disclosed gradiometer system includes one or more magnetic sensors and an actuation module configured to vary the sensing positions of the magnetic sensors. During operation, the actuation module changes the sensing positions over time in accordance with a predetermined displacement function, thereby enabling magnetic-field measurements to be acquired at multiple spatial locations.

A controller receives readout data from the magnetic sensors during a measurement period. The readout data represents the magnetic field detected at the varying sensing positions. The controller processes the readout data to generate a differential magnetic-field time profile by determining differences between magnetic-field measurements obtained at two or more of the sensing positions. The controller then demodulates the differential magnetic-field time profile using the predetermined displacement function. Based on this demodulation, the controller determines at least one vector component of the magnetic-field gradient.
outputs.L4:
A gradiometer system includes one or more magnetic-field sensors and a displacement mechanism configured to move the sensors among predetermined sensing positions. The displacement mechanism may translate, rotate, oscillate, or otherwise vary the position of each sensor according to a defined displacement function. At each sensing position, the sensors generate readouts representing one or more vector components of the local magnetic field.

A processing unit receives the sensor readouts and combines measurements obtained at different sensing positions to produce a differential magnetic-field profile. By comparing measurements associated with known spatial separations, the processing unit suppresses common-mode magnetic-field contributions and isolates field variations attributable to a magnetic-field gradient. The differential profile is then demodulated using the displacement function, so that the measured temporal modulation can be related to the corresponding spatial variation of the magnetic field.

The resulting output is a time-dependent profile of at least one vector component of the magnetic-field gradient. Because the sensing positions may be varied dynamically, the system can adjust the effective measurement baseline, sampling pattern, orientation, or spatial resolution during operation. In this manner, magnetic-field gradients can be measured without requiring a permanently fixed arrangement of spatially separated sensors, while retaining a known relationship between sensor displacement and the derived gradient signal.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a gradiometer system that mechanically varies magnetic sensor positions and demodulates differential field measurements to determine a magnetic-field gradient.
counterfactuals.output: A gradiometer system includes first and second magnetic-field sensors, a mechanical actuator configured to vary a relative position of at least one sensor, and a controller coupled to the sensors and actuator. The actuator periodically changes a separation, orientation, or spatial location of the sensors according to a modulation waveform, thereby modulating differential magnetic-field measurements obtained at multiple sensor positions. The controller receives sensor signals, determines a differential field signal, and synchronously demodulates the differential field signal using a reference associated with the modulation waveform. A magnetic-field gradient is determined from the demodulated signal and a corresponding displacement or baseline between the sensor positions. Common-mode magnetic fields, sensor offsets, drift, and low-frequency noise may be suppressed by the mechanical modulation and synchronous demodulation. The system may further compensate for actuator motion, sensor gain, phase delay, and higher-order spatial-field components to generate one- or multi-axis gradient measurements.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for measuring a vector component of a magnetic field gradient using one or more movable magnetic sensors, a predetermined time-dependent displacement function, and a controller that processes and demodulates sensor readout data.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention for measuring a selected vector component of a magnetic-field gradient comprises:

- **One or more magnetic-field sensors** responsive to a selected field component;
- **A motion mechanism** that moves each sensor along a known direction according to a predetermined time-dependent displacement function \( \mathbf{x}(t) \), such as a sinusoidal, triangular, or coded periodic trajectory; and
- **A controller** that synchronizes the motion with acquisition of the sensor readout and demodulates the acquired data using the known displacement function.

For a sensor displaced about a nominal position \(\mathbf{x}_0\), its output is approximately

\[
B_i(\mathbf{x}_0+\mathbf{x}(t))
\approx B_i(\mathbf{x}_0)
+\sum_j \frac{\partial B_i}{\partial x_j}x_j(t).
\]

Thus, motion in direction \(j\) modulates the gradient component \(\partial B_i/\partial x_j\) into a time-varying sensor signal. The controller removes or rejects the static-field term and performs synchronous, lock-in, correlation, or matched-filter demodulation against \(x_j(t)\). The resulting demodulated amplitude, divided by the calibrated displacement amplitude and sensor sensitivity, provides the desired vector component of the magnetic-field gradient.

Multiple sensors may be moved together, oppositely, or with different phases. Their outputs can be combined to suppress uniform-field drift, vibration artifacts, offsets, and common-mode interference, while permitting simultaneous or sequential recovery of multiple gradient-tensor components. Position feedback and calibration data may be used by the controller to compensate for imperfect motion, sensor gain, phase delay, and trajectory nonlinearity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical disclosure of a magnetic gradiometer comprising an actuation module, magnetic sensors, and a controller configured to calculate field gradients from measurements taken at varied sensing positions.
counterfactuals.output: A magnetic gradiometer includes an actuation module, one or more magnetic-field sensors coupled to the actuation module, and a controller in communication with the sensors and actuation module. The actuation module selectively positions the sensors at a plurality of spatially separated sensing positions according to a predetermined or adaptive motion sequence. At each sensing position, the controller acquires magnetic-field measurements and associates the measurements with corresponding position data. The controller calculates one or more spatial magnetic-field gradients from differences among the measurements and the known separations between sensing positions. Measurements may be time synchronized, averaged, and corrected for sensor offset, motion-induced error, and environmental drift. By obtaining measurements at varied positions using the same sensor or a calibrated sensor array, the gradiometer reduces common-mode error and provides gradient estimates along one or more axes.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you formulate a patent abstract for a system that moves magnetic sensing locations according to a known displacement profile, computes a differential magnetic-field time profile, and demodulates it to recover the magnetic-field gradient?
counterfactuals.output: A magnetic-field sensing system includes one or more magnetic sensors, a positioning mechanism configured to move magnetic sensing locations according to a predetermined displacement profile, and a processor. The processor receives magnetic-field measurements acquired at the moving sensing locations and computes a differential magnetic-field time profile representing differences between measurements associated with spatially separated sensing locations. Using the predetermined displacement profile as a demodulation reference, the processor demodulates the differential magnetic-field time profile to recover a magnetic-field gradient, including a magnitude, direction, or spatial component thereof. The displacement profile may be periodic and may define the time-varying separation or orientation of the sensing locations. Synchronous demodulation can distinguish displacement-correlated gradient signals from common-mode magnetic fields, sensor offsets, and noise. The recovered magnetic-field gradient may be used for magnetic anomaly detection, localization, navigation, imaging, or characterization of a magnetic source.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
